report.title: Anthropic files confidential S-1, eyes public markets ahead of OpenAI
report.summary: Anthropic submitted a draft S-1 to the SEC on June 1, 2026, kicking off the race to go public before OpenAI. Run-rate revenue has crossed $30B, up from $9B at end of 2025, and the company carries a $965B post-money valuation from its $65B Series H.

report.title: Claude Opus 4.8 ships as default on Max, Team Premium, and Anthropic API
report.summary: Anthropic released Opus 4.8 with improvements over Opus 4.7 in coding, agentic skills, reasoning, and knowledge work. It is now the default model in Claude Code on Max and Team Premium plans; Opus 4.1 is deprecated and retiring August 5.

report.title: Anthropic ships self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels for Claude Managed Agents
report.summary: Claude Managed Agents now support self-hosted sandboxes (public beta) that run tool execution inside your own infrastructure or managed providers like Cloudflare, Modal, or Vercel, while Anthropic handles orchestration. MCP tunnels (research preview) let agents reach private-network MCP servers without exposing public endpoints.

report.title: Microsoft Build 2026: seven in-house MAI models, agent runtime, and Majorana 2 chip
report.summary: Microsoft shipped seven in-house AI models (MAI-Thinking-1, MAI-Code-1-Flash, MAI-Image-2.5, and others) trained without OpenAI involvement, plus Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA, Microsoft Execution Containers for sandboxed agent code, and the Majorana 2 quantum chip targeting a million-qubit path by 2029. Foundry model catalog now hosts 11,000+ models.

report.title: Google retires Gemini CLI for consumer users, ships Antigravity CLI
report.summary: Google announced Antigravity CLI as the successor to Gemini CLI, built in Go for faster execution and async multi-agent workflows. Gemini CLI stops serving Google AI Pro/Ultra requests on June 18, 2026; enterprise Gemini Code Assist licenses are unaffected.

report.title: OpenAI Codex CLI ships multi-agent v2, plugin sharing, and remote-control pairing
report.summary: June Codex CLI releases added multi-agent v2 (each thread keeps its own runtime choice), workspace plugin sharing for Enterprise, and remote-control pairing via app-server v2 RPCs. The CLI is open-source, built in Rust, and backed by GPT-5.5.

report.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft CEOs urge Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening
report.summary: The heads of four leading AI labs signed a joint letter on June 5 calling for mandatory biosecurity screening of all synthetic DNA providers in the US, arguing that AI now lowers the expertise threshold for misuse of biological material.

learn.name: Claude Code Dynamic Workflows
learn.oneLineDescription: Spawn hundreds of parallel sub-agents from Claude Code for large codebase tasks.

detail.whatItDoes:
Dynamic Workflows is a Claude Code feature (available in v2.1.154+) where Claude writes an orchestration script for your task and then fans it out across many background sub-agents running in parallel. Each sub-agent operates in an isolated context window and reports back to a lead agent that synthesizes findings. You trigger a workflow with /workflows and manage runs from the same interface.

Use cases include codebase-wide security audits, large framework migrations, incident post-mortems where sub-agents fan out through deploy history, error logs, metrics, and support tickets simultaneously. The full execution trace is visible in Claude Console — every sub-agent's actions, ordering, and reasoning are inspectable.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform engineers, senior developers, and teams running large codebase migrations or multi-file audits who have previously had to wire together custom orchestration code to parallelize Claude tasks. Requires a Max, Team Premium, or Enterprise plan with Opus 4.8 as the default model.
pros: Parallelizes tasks that would previously require custom orchestration scripts
Full audit trail in Claude Console — every sub-agent action is inspectable
Works with self-hosted sandboxes (public beta) so code never leaves your perimeter
Automatically handles context management and error recovery across sub-agents
cons: Token costs scale linearly with sub-agent count — large workflows can be expensive fast
Requires Opus 4.8 (v2.1.154+); older versions will not support /workflows
Still early — complex dependency graphs between sub-agents are not yet natively modeled
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Code v2.1.154 or later (`claude --version`)
- Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, or Anthropic API plan
- Opus 4.8 set as your active model

## Step 1: Update Claude Code

```bash
npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
claude --version  # should show 2.1.154 or later
```

## Step 2: Set Opus 4.8 as your model

Inside a Claude Code session:

```
/model opus-4-8
```

Or pin it in your project settings file `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "claude-opus-4-8-20260601",
  "effort": "high"
}
```

For harder tasks, bump effort:

```
/effort xhigh
```

## Step 3: Trigger a workflow

Navigate to your project root and start Claude Code:

```bash
cd your-project
claude
```

Describe a large task naturally — Claude will decide if a workflow is appropriate:

```
> Audit every file in src/ for SQL injection vulnerabilities, then generate a patch for each one found.
```

Or explicitly manage workflows:

```
/workflows          # list active and past workflow runs
/workflows status   # check sub-agent progress
```

## Gotcha: Token cost

Workflows spawn many sub-agents, each with its own context. A codebase-wide audit on a large repo can consume 10–50M tokens. Check your usage in Claude Console before kicking off wide searches. Use `/effort high` (not `xhigh`) for exploratory passes to limit per-sub-agent thinking budget.

## Step 4 (optional): Enable self-hosted sandboxes

For teams that need code to stay in their perimeter, enroll in the public beta via Claude Console under **Settings > Managed Agents > Sandboxes**, then point execution at your own infrastructure (Cloudflare, Modal, Vercel, or a custom endpoint).

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source, Rust-built terminal coding agent from OpenAI backed by GPT-5.5.

detail.whatItDoes:
Codex CLI is OpenAI's terminal coding agent. It runs locally, can read and modify files in your working directory, and executes shell commands. It is built in Rust for speed, is open source (github.com/openai/codex), and is backed by GPT-5.5. It supports multi-agent v2 (each spawned thread keeps its own model runtime choice), plugin sharing for Enterprise workspaces, remote-control pairing so a colleague can attach to your session, and sandboxed code execution.

The June 2026 releases added multi-agent v2 with cleaner follow-up defaults for spawned agents, machine-readable `codex plugin list --json` output, hosted web and image tools inside code-mode flows, and standalone parallel web searches.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who want a ChatGPT-account-backed coding agent in the terminal without leaving OpenAI's ecosystem. ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans include Codex access. Teams on Enterprise get workspace-level plugin sharing so teammates can install shared local plugins from the Codex plugin directory.
pros: Open source (Apache 2.0) — inspect and extend the Rust source
Backed by GPT-5.5, which scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0
Multi-agent v2 supports parallel sub-agent threads each with independent runtime choices
Single install script works on macOS, Linux, and Windows
cons: Tightly coupled to GPT-5.5 — no support for non-OpenAI models
Requires a paid ChatGPT plan; free tier does not include Codex
Windows sandbox support is still alpha (`codex sandbox setup --elevated`)
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS or Linux (Windows alpha available)
- ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan
- No other dependencies — the installer is self-contained

## Step 1: Install

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Alternatively, install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install openai-codex
```

## Step 2: Authenticate

```bash
codex login
# Opens browser — sign in with your ChatGPT account
# Or use an API key:
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
```

## Step 3: Run in your project

```bash
cd your-project
codex
```

Code-mode with a single prompt (non-interactive):
```bash
codex -p "Add input validation to every POST endpoint in src/routes/"
```

## Step 4: Enable plugins (Enterprise)

List installed plugins:
```bash
codex plugin list --json
```

Install a plugin from the marketplace:
```bash
codex plugin install <plugin-name>
```

Share a plugin with your workspace so teammates can install it:
```bash
codex plugin share <plugin-name>
```

## Gotcha: Unattended / CI installs

Set `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` before running the installer in CI to skip all prompts:
```bash
export CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
```

Then authenticate via API key rather than browser OAuth:
```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
codex -p "Run the test suite and report failures" --output-format json
```

learn.name: Gemini CLI (google-gemini/gemini-cli)
learn.oneLineDescription: Free, open-source terminal AI agent with 1M-token context and 1,000 req/day free tier.

detail.whatItDoes:
Gemini CLI is Google's open-source (Apache 2.0) terminal AI agent. It uses a ReAct (reason-and-act) loop with built-in tools — file operations, shell commands, web fetching, and Google Search grounding — plus MCP support for custom integrations. The free tier with a personal Google account gives 60 req/min and 1,000 req/day against Gemini models with a 1M-token context window.

Note: Google announced at I/O 2026 that Gemini CLI will transition to Antigravity CLI for consumer users by June 18, 2026. Gemini CLI continues to work for paid Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise license holders. If you are on a free Google account, plan to migrate to Antigravity CLI. The install and usage commands below work today for the Gemini CLI stable release.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who want a free, zero-lock-in terminal AI agent for everyday coding tasks, long-context codebase reads, or Google Cloud-native automation. Also a strong choice for teams already on Vertex AI — authentication integrates cleanly with existing IAM. On hard multi-file refactors, Claude Code still leads on SWE-bench Verified; for free exploration and long-context reads, Gemini CLI is the most cost-effective starting point.
pros: Genuinely free: 1,000 req/day with a personal Google account, no credit card required
1M-token context window beats most competitors' defaults by 2.5-7x
Open source under Apache 2.0 — inspect, fork, and contribute
Built-in Google Search grounding directly inside the agent loop
cons: Transitioning to Antigravity CLI for consumer users on June 18 — new installs of Gemini CLI will not receive feature updates
Scores ~12 points behind Claude Opus 4.7 on SWE-bench Verified for hard multi-file refactors
The --yolo auto-approve flag will execute any shell command without confirmation — avoid outside a sandbox
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node.js 18 or later (`node --version`)
- A Google account (for the free tier)

## Step 1: Install

```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
```

Or run without installing:
```bash
npx @google/gemini-cli
```

## Step 2: Authenticate

**Personal Google account (free tier — 1,000 req/day):**
```bash
gemini login
# Opens browser — sign in with your Google account
```

**API key (pay-as-you-go, no daily cap):**
```bash
# Get a key at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIza..."
```

**Vertex AI (enterprise/GCP):**
```bash
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true
gemini
```

## Step 3: Run in your project

```bash
cd your-project
gemini
```

Single-shot prompt:
```bash
gemini -p "Explain the architecture of this codebase"
```

Attach a specific file:
```bash
gemini -f src/auth.ts -p "Review this for security issues"
```

Headless/CI mode:
```bash
gemini --headless -p "Run tests and report failures" --output-format json
```

## Step 4: Per-project config

Create a `GEMINI.md` at your project root to give persistent context:
```markdown
# Project Context
This is a Django 5.x API. Always use type hints. Tests use pytest.
```

Gemini CLI reads this file automatically at session start.

## Gotchas

**`command not found: gemini`** — npm global bin is not on your PATH.
```bash
npm config get prefix
# Add $prefix/bin to your shell profile, e.g.:
echo 'export PATH="$(npm config get prefix)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

**`EACCES` on `npm install -g`** — Switch to nvm or run:
```bash
npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global
export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
```

**Migration to Antigravity CLI (June 18+):** Enterprise/paid users stay on Gemini CLI. Free users should follow Google's migration guide at developers.googleblog.com.

learn.name: MAI-Thinking-1 on Microsoft Foundry
learn.oneLineDescription: Microsoft's first in-house reasoning model: 35B active params, 256K context, private preview on Foundry.

detail.whatItDoes:
MAI-Thinking-1 is the flagship model from Microsoft's seven-model MAI family, shipped at Build 2026. It is a 35B active-parameter reasoning model with a 256K context window, trained from scratch without distillation from any third-party model on enterprise-grade, commercially licensed data. Microsoft claims it matches Claude Opus 4.6 on SWE-bench Pro coding benchmarks and was preferred over Claude Sonnet 4.6 in blind evaluations — though these results have not been independently verified.

The model is currently in private preview on Azure Foundry (formerly Azure AI Studio). Access requires a Foundry workspace and an approved private-preview enrollment. It is model-agnostic in the sense that the same Foundry endpoint and billing relationship works for all 11,000+ models in the catalog, including OpenAI GPT-5.5 and Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8/Sonnet 4.5.
detail.whoItsFor: Enterprise teams already in the Azure ecosystem who need a reasoning model with clean data provenance for compliance-sensitive workloads. The low-token-cost positioning also makes it a candidate for high-volume agentic pipelines where GPT-5.5 costs are prohibitive. Not yet suitable for teams that need a stable public GA model — private preview status means availability and API shape can change.
pros: Trained on commercially licensed data with auditable provenance — relevant for regulated industries
256K context window at reportedly low token cost compared to GPT-5.5
Same Foundry endpoint and billing for all 11,000+ catalog models — no additional integration work
Model Router can auto-switch between MAI-Thinking-1 and other models at runtime for cost/performance
cons: Private preview only — no guaranteed SLA, API shape may change before GA
Microsoft's benchmark claims (vs Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6) are self-reported and not independently verified
Requires Azure Foundry workspace setup and private-preview enrollment — not accessible in minutes
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Azure subscription with an active resource group
- Azure CLI installed (`az --version`) and authenticated (`az login`)
- Private-preview enrollment for MAI-Thinking-1 (request at https://aka.ms/MAI-Thinking-1-preview)

## Step 1: Create a Foundry project

```bash
# Install the Azure AI Foundry SDK
pip install azure-ai-projects azure-identity

# Create a Foundry hub and project via CLI
az ml workspace create \
  --name my-foundry-project \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --kind hub
```

Or navigate to https://ai.azure.com and create a new project under your subscription.

## Step 2: Deploy MAI-Thinking-1

In the Foundry portal:
1. Go to **Model catalog** → search `MAI-Thinking-1`
2. Click **Deploy** → choose **Serverless (pay-as-you-go)**
3. Name your deployment (e.g., `mai-thinking-1-prod`)
4. Copy the **endpoint URL** and **API key** from the deployment page

## Step 3: Call the endpoint

```python
import os
from openai import AzureOpenAI

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint=os.environ["AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT"],
    api_key=os.environ["AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY"],
    api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="mai-thinking-1-prod",  # your deployment name
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior software engineer."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Review this Python function for edge cases: ..."}
    ],
    max_tokens=4096,
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Step 4: Use Model Router for automatic fallback

```python
# Point at the Foundry Model Router endpoint instead of a specific deployment
client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint=os.environ["AZURE_FOUNDRY_ROUTER_ENDPOINT"],
    api_key=os.environ["AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY"],
    api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
)
# Model Router picks MAI-Thinking-1 for reasoning tasks, Flash models for simple queries
```

## Gotcha: Private preview gating

MAI-Thinking-1 will return a `404` or `ModelNotFound` error if your subscription has not been approved for private preview. The enrollment link is https://aka.ms/MAI-Thinking-1-preview. Approvals have been taking 3-5 business days as of Build week.
